rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the context. The two-provider approach suggested above supports this scenario: register one hover provider that returns Content A immediately and another that returns a promise resolving to Content B, both covering the same range. The hover incorporates provider results as they become available, so Content A can appear before Content B finishes while the hover remains open. rows.proposedComment:

rows.title: [Bug] After switching the model, the placeholder does not disappear
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the complete example. The current editor-core source explains this: placeholder visibility observes the model's version ID, but not model identity, so switching between two newly created models with the same version ID can retain the previous visibility state. Passing through a null model changes that dependency, which explains your workaround. The editor-core defect should be filed at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues; this Monaco report should remain open until the fix reaches a Monaco release.

rows.title: [Bug] Cut Event from context menu has event type 'copy'
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the reproduction and clarification. The current editor core uses a copy command followed by selection deletion for context-menu Cut when EditContext is enabled, which explains the copy event you're observing. This is an EditContext workaround, so the event behavior needs review without breaking cutting. The relevant implementation belongs in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues; we'll keep this report open pending that review.

[CVE-2026-0540] DOMPurify contains a Cross-site Scripting vulnerability
[Bug] Error when hovering over invalid `:nth-child` instruction
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the focused playground reproduction. This traces to the bundled vscode-css-languageservice: its selector-specificity hover code handles `:nth-child` when the parse node has children, but then reads `childElements[1].getText()` without ensuring that expression exists. Monaco's CSS worker delegates hover calculation directly to that service, so this should remain open as an upstream issue until the language service guards the malformed selector and Monaco consumes the resulting release.
